items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — went straight from greeting into the purpose of the call
Never stated the hourly rate per mover per hour — only gave a total dollar budget range ($714-$918), so the customer has no idea what the rate actually is
No 'pricing is super simple' framing or any structured pricing walkthrough
Never listed what's included in the rate (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools)
Disassembly / reassembly not mentioned, despite a dresser and a one-bedroom's furniture in scope
On-Time Guarantee never pitched — she gave a 30-minute arrival window but never said Einstein starts discounting if the window is missed
No 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees)
Packing needs never probed and packing service pricing never offered
Never asked the moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no prep-equals-shorter-move framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip
Confirmation email described but not explained — no bolded-details-at-top, no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask
Never gave office hours or how to reach the team
Walk distance and assembly/disassembly confirmed during probing but never explained back as time variables in the estimate
No 60 cents/lb baseline paired with the No Worries coverage explanation
Customer's name pronounced three different ways across the call (Kaleen / Kallen / Caitlin) and never corrected
top_strength: Very efficient, well-sequenced discovery — in under seven minutes she confirmed both addresses, floors, unit numbers, garage contents, heavy/valuable items, TVs, box count and walk distances, then used that detail to correct the online estimate up from 3.5 hours to a 3.5-4.5 hour range with specific reasoning (first floor, garage items, second floor with no elevator, 25 minutes of drive time).
coaching_note: She quoted a dollar range without ever saying the hourly rate — the customer heard '$714 to $918' with no idea what an hour costs, which makes the bill feel arbitrary if the move runs long. Pair every estimate with the rate per mover per hour, what that rate already includes, and the no-hidden-fees list, then run the Save Your Ass prep speech (consolidate the garage boxes and Christmas decorations, take a carload of loose items) — on this exact move that speech is the difference between the 3.5-hour end and the 4.5-hour end of her own range.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and steady but heavily scripted — 'Awesome' used as the transition after nearly every answer, no empathy markers or rapport moments, and the customer stayed monosyllabic throughout.
